summary: Stratos opens with a real sign-in page that can be skipped for now, keeps a phone's live tracking inside the app instead of opening the PC's address, and detects the aircraft itself.
releaseNotes: Opening Stratos for the first time shows a sign-in page with two choices, Sign in or Create account, and a Skip for now button that leaves the whole app working without an account.

A complete account flow: full name, username, email, password with confirmation and a strength meter, a Terms and Privacy checkbox the account service enforces, and automatic sign-in to the map after registering.
Remember me keeps a device signed in for 30 days; without it the session ends after twelve hours or when the tab closes.
Settings opens with a Stratos account card that names the signed-in pilot, offers Sign in or create an account when the prompt was skipped, and signs out.
A signed-in PC publishes its live flight to the account, so a phone opens Stratos's own live view by itself: no address, no second browser tab, no taps.
Signing in returns to the page that asked for it, or the map, and a signed-in visitor never sees the sign-in page again.
The first-launch page follows the existing dark navy and cyan design, with subtle motion, and is responsive on desktop, tablet and phone.
The Flight Deck, live map, EFB, logbook, pilot and weather pages ask for an account; the bridge's own LAN pages stay exempt, and Skip keeps the desktop app usable offline.
Aircraft identity is detected automatically from X-Plane's datarefs and the MSFS title, so there is nothing to type before flying.
Username validation now matches the account service at three characters instead of promising two.
The PC-map offer and its Open PC map button are gone, so a phone never follows a LAN address that may be switched off.
Sign-up reports a duplicate email or a taken username without losing what was typed.
The manual Aircraft identity card was removed, along with the bridge-save step it needed.
The account service must be updated with this release: it adds the full-name and terms columns to the account database (relay/worker/migrations/002-name-and-terms.sql).
Automatic phone tracking needs the PC signed in with live publishing left on. A phone that skipped the account keeps the local map, logbook and EFB but cannot follow the PC.
Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages are now published and linked from sign-up.
